cases.grading_note: No violation beyond baseline (baseline at the pin is empty). Import-form probe (verified in the post-augment graph): the plain whole-module form 'import tuf.api.metadata' registers IMPORTS tuf.repository._dotted -> tuf.api.metadata verbatim (import_statement records the full dotted target), which satisfies ADR-0010's requires for the appended load_role_metadata; the function's attribute-chain call also registers CALLS onto tuf.api.metadata.Metadata.from_file. This is the discriminating counterpart to tuf-bench-legacy-json-store: same added-file shape, but the dotted import form alone flips the requires from fire to satisfied. If a future change stopped recording plain-import targets, this case would flip to a fire and catch it.

expected_violations.subject: tuf.repository.*
expected_violations.justification: ADR-0010 ('Repository library design built on top of Metadata API'): the repository library is built on top of the Metadata API, and the gold constraint reads 'the repository library is built on top of the Metadata API; this is a dependency'. The added module performs repository maintenance work through the Repository ABC alone; its only import binds the class node tuf.repository.Repository, and class nodes carry no dependency edges toward the metadata package (method CALLS attach to method FQNs), so the class scope has no dependency path to tuf.api.metadata.* at any scope and the requires fires. Verified firing empirically at the pin (2026-09-15): exactly one violation, at the class FQN (refresh_snapshot dedups beneath it).

cases.grading_note: Single exact firing at the class FQN. Mechanism: walk_imports resolves the from-import to the known class FQN (module_name + imported preferred when known), and BFS from a class node dead-ends (its methods' edges live on method FQNs), the same dead-end that makes the eval's __init__.py case fire (tuf/repository/__init__.py:13 imports the classes AbortEdit/Repository, never the module). If a future change attached method-level dependency edges to the enclosing class (or treated class imports as package facade hops), this case and the facade case below would flip to satisfied — that semantics change is exactly what this pair pins. Instance-disjoint from every other case (only case binding _via_repository).

expected_violations.subject: tuf.repository.*
expected_violations.justification: ADR-0010 ('Repository library design built on top of Metadata API'): the repository library is built on top of the Metadata API. The added module leans on the repository package facade without any Metadata API dependency of its own; the plain import records the verbatim target tuf.repository, and BFS continues from the package node — but the package's only dependency edges are the class-target imports of AbortEdit and Repository (tuf/repository/__init__.py:13), which are dead-ends, so the path never reaches tuf.api.metadata.* and the requires fires at the appended function. cases.grading_note: Single exact firing at the function FQN. This case started life as a compliant probe on the prediction that a 2-hop IMPORTS path (facade -> _repository -> tuf.api.metadata) would satisfy the requires; the empirical run refuted the prediction — the hop never reaches _repository the MODULE because __init__.py imports its classes, not the module. Together with tuf-bench-probe-repository-sibling-import (module-target hop, satisfied) and tuf-bench-repository-class-import (class-target, fires) this is the reachability-boundary triad for requires satisfaction: which hop target a repository module imports decides satisfaction, and the answer is module nodes yes, class nodes and class-only facades no. Any additional firing (e.g. ADR-0006) on this module is a false positive: the module is outside the tuf.api.metadata.* subject. Instance-disjoint from every other case (only case binding _via_package).

    """Summarize the repository implementation module for docs (new code)."""

cases.grading_note: No violation beyond baseline (baseline at the pin is empty; verified 2026-09-15). The plain import records the verbatim module target tuf.repository._repository, whose own module-level import (tuf/repository/_repository.py:15, from tuf.api.metadata import ...) carries the BFS path to the requires' object, so the appended function is satisfied TRANSITIVELY — the fresh-module counterpart of the module-seeding probes: satisfaction here rides a sibling module's edges, not the enclosing module's. Discriminating contrast within the triad: same plain-import form as the facade case, but the module target satisfies where the class-only facade fires. If transitive satisfaction for requires were ever removed (per-function-usage semantics, issue 124 option b family), this probe flips to a fire — that is the regression it guards. Instance-disjoint from every other case (only case binding _via_sibling).

cases.description: Deletion of the serialization package's __init__.py (the ADR-0006 requires' object side): records that requires cannot detect its dependency being deleted — the fire never moves to the depending module
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected (verified 2026-09-15), and that silence IS the finding. process_diff handles deleted files: the old bytes are parsed and every def in the deleted __init__.py (plus the module) becomes a deleted-type changed FQN. But requires predicates fire only when a changed FQN matches the constraint SUBJECT (tuf.api.metadata.* / tuf.repository.*); the deleted FQNs live under tuf.api.serialization, the OBJECT side, and tuf/api/metadata.py itself is unchanged so nothing re-evaluates its satisfaction — the requires on the metadata module cannot detect that its dependency was just removed. Second limitation layered on top: augment_adg cannot remove nodes, so the merged graph still carries the serialization nodes (the HA removal case documents the staged-tree workaround for prohibits-side deletions; here even that would not help, because the blindness is subject-side). This case type records the deletion-side recall ceiling for the benchmark report; if subject-revalidation-on-object-deletion ever lands, this expectation flips and the case must be re-authored as type injected.

cases.description: Hand-rolled JSON envelope class appended inside tuf/api/metadata.py itself: resolves the 'fresh-module ADR-0006 fire' proposal — no fresh module can ever match the subject, and appended scopes inside metadata.py are uniformly seeded, so ADR-0006 has zero fireable instances at this pin
cases.grading_note: No violation beyond baseline (baseline at the pin is empty; verified 2026-09-15). Resolution of the 2026-09-14 edge-case proposal 'fresh-module ADR-0006 fire outside metadata.py seeding': impossible by construction. The subject tuf.api.metadata.* matches only the defs inside tuf/api/metadata.py (a module, not a package — no fresh file can produce an FQN under it), and every scope inside that module is satisfied under uniform seeding (#115/#124a) by the module's own serialization dependency (the module-level TYPE_CHECKING/serializer imports plus the CALLS edge to tuf.api.serialization.json that the bare-json resolver quirk registers). The appended LegacyJsonEnvelope therefore stays silent despite hand-rolling JSON exactly as ADR-0006's rejected option 1 describes — this probe documents ADR-0006 as un-fireable at any pin, the constraint-side counterpart of the historical_pins analysis (499f1c85^ / 22b27264 rejected for the same mask). If per-function-usage satisfaction (issue 124 option b) ever landed, this probe flips to a fire and ADR-0006 becomes fireable; that is the regression it guards. The appended function-local 'import json' must stay quiet under ADR-0001 (prohibits python2.7/python3.5 only).

cases.description: New stdlib-json helper appended inside tuf/repository/_repository.py: the module's own Metadata API import satisfies the appended scope even though the function itself only touches json (discriminating probe of module-import seeding)
cases.grading_note: No violation beyond baseline (baseline at the pin is empty): tuf/repository/_repository.py imports tuf.api.metadata at module level (tuf/repository/_repository.py:15), so ADR-0010's requires is satisfied for the appended _parse_role_bytes via enclosing-module seeding (#115) even though the function itself never touches the Metadata API. Instance-disjointness within the shared file: the eval's _repository.py case is a zero-expectation probe appending a bare _helper(): pass; this case appends a stdlib-json-using function, so the diff and the changed FQN differ. The case discriminates a per-function-usage satisfaction semantics (issue 124 option b): such a change would flip this probe to a fire, and any ADR-0010 firing today means the #115 seeding regressed and counts as an over-trigger false positive.
